verification_note: All 6 surviving findings independently re-verified against the detached worktree at the reviewed sha.

findings.title: Reset-arm rt_landlord_id grep guard pin is not unique to the reset arm — it also matches the pre-existing consent-reject arm, so the guard cannot detect a revert of the change it was added to protect
findings.evidence: Guard pin (both chains): 'document.cookie="rt_landlord_id=; Max-Age=0; Path=/; SameSite=Lax";rtPhId=null' — occurs 3x per chain: (1) the NEW reset arm 'document.cookie="rt_ph_reset=; Max-Age=0; Path=/; SameSite=Lax";document.cookie="rt_landlord_id=; Max-Age=0; Path=/; SameSite=Lax";rtPhId=null;window.posthog.reset()', (2) the PRE-EXISTING consent-reject arm 'window.posthog.opt_out_capturing();document.cookie="rt_landlord_id=; Max-Age=0; Path=/; SameSite=Lax";rtPhId=null;}}', (3) the pin itself.
findings.detail: The pinned substring was already satisfied by the pre-existing consent-changed opt-out branch before this PR. Reverting only the new reset-arm clear would still pass both build guards — the regression the guard claims to defend (stale landlord re-identify after logout within the 60s window) is not actually pinned.
findings.recommended_fix: Pin the reset-arm adjacency in BOTH guard lists (Makefile ~274 and Dockerfile ~133): 'rt_ph_reset=; Max-Age=0; Path=/; SameSite=Lax";document.cookie="rt_landlord_id=' — verified to occur exactly once per chain.

findings.title: Advisory test gate: CONCERNS
findings.evidence: P0 surfaces (server-side identify+capture, signup_completed/login_succeeded polarity off (xmax=0), cookie Max-Age=60/10) are FULL: oauth_first_signin_fires_identify_and_signup_completed_test + oauth_returning_signin_fires_login_succeeded_test drive complete_oauth_flow against the real DB and assert both polarities; external_id_cookie_test.gleam pins Max-Age=60 (identify) and Max-Age=10 (both sentinels). P1 gap: the reset-arm snippet change has zero effective regression coverage because the grep pin is not unique (see coverage-gap finding).
findings.detail: P0 100%, P1 ~80% (reset-arm regression coverage effectively none), overall ~90% — CONCERNS band. Critical OAuth funnel is solid; one load-bearing privacy surface has no test that would fail on regression.
findings.recommended_fix: Fix the reset-arm grep pin to be unique (see coverage-gap finding); optionally add a bug-hunt assertion that rt_landlord_id is absent immediately after logout.

findings.title: OAuth insert-vs-update detection relies on the undocumented PostgreSQL xmax MVCC field (PG-internal, not a stable SQL contract)
findings.evidence: (xmax = 0) AS is_new — comment: 'a freshly INSERTed row has xmax = 0 (no deleting/updating transaction); a DO UPDATE row carries the updater's txid. Lets the caller distinguish a first OAuth sign-in from a returning one atomically — no check-then-act race.'
findings.detail: The idiom is correct and atomic today (integration tests exercise both polarities), and the SQL comment documents the semantics — but the lens's 'undocumented' framing is only partly right: the comment explains behavior, not that xmax semantics are PG-internal and could change on a major-version upgrade.
findings.recommended_fix: No change required. Optionally add a one-line 'PG-internal, re-verify on Postgres major upgrade' caveat to the SQL comment.

findings.title: OAuth sign-in now sends landlord email to PostHog server-side with no analytics-consent gate — matches the in-production email/password posture
findings.evidence: posthog_client.identify_with_set_once(posthog, row.id, [#("email", json.string(row.email))], ...) — no consent gate precedes it; compare process_signup at :258-262 which is explicitly documented 'Consent-independent — these are first-party URL params the SPA carried in-memory, not the consent-gated browser trackers.'
findings.detail: Email PII is transmitted to a third-party processor (PostHog) on every Google sign-in without a consent check. This exactly mirrors the pre-existing email/password signup and login paths (the documented precedent), and the code comment discloses the OAuth-scoped capture. Recorded for the privacy/consent record; not a deviation.
findings.recommended_fix: No code change if the posture is intentional (it is — email/password is the precedent). Confirm the documented privacy posture covers server-side PII transmission to PostHog across both auth paths.

findings.title: OAuth path calls identify_with_set_once with an all-empty FirstTouch — behaviorally identify/3, contradicts the function's own 'prefer identify/3' guidance
findings.evidence: attribution.first_touch_set_once(attribution.FirstTouch(utm_source: "", utm_medium: "", ...)) — first_touch_set_once filters empties and returns [] (attribution.gleam:59-80: 'Returns `[]` when nothing survives'), so the call is behaviorally identify/3. posthog_client.identify_with_set_once doc: 'Pass `[]` for set_once_properties and prefer `identify/3` when there is nothing write-once to record.'
findings.detail: Deliberate and documented in the code comment (mirrors the signup path's call shape so first-touch persistence can drop in later), but it routes an empty object through the attribution masking/clamping function. Minor style deviation from the module's own guidance.
findings.recommended_fix: Acceptable as-is (documented intent). If strict: call posthog_client.identify/3 directly and note the signup-shape mirror in the comment.

findings.title: complete_oauth_flow made pub for tests widens the in-process session-forgery boundary below the PKCE exchange
findings.evidence: 'pub fn complete_oauth_flow(...) -> Response' with doc: 'Public so integration tests can drive the funnel with a fabricated OAuthTokenResponse — the PKCE exchange above it needs a live Supabase.' The function upserts a landlord and sets session cookies from an unvalidated token_resp.
findings.detail: Any future server module could call it to forge a session, bypassing PKCE. Not reachable from HTTP directly (route handlers call process_oauth_callback, which performs the token exchange), the server is a monolith, and Gleam has no test-only visibility — the doc comment mitigates but does not enforce.
findings.recommended_fix: Acceptable as-is given the constraints. If tighter: keep private and expose a clearly-named test seam, or inject the token exchange as a parameter.

verdict_justification: 0 blockers. All load-bearing surfaces verified sound: (xmax=0) is_new is the canonical atomic insert-vs-update idiom with correct polarity and both polarities integration-tested; the 4-place snippet contract is satisfied (reset-arm clear present in both Makefile and Dockerfile chains); cookie lifetimes are correct (identify 60s, sentinels 10s) with matching unit assertions and no stragglers; identify+capture mirror the email/password signup path exactly, consent-independent by the same documented precedent, and the anonymous→identified merge link (rt_landlord_id cookie) is preserved. 2 warnings: the new reset-arm guard pin is not unique (also matches the pre-existing consent-reject arm) so it cannot detect a revert of the change it protects — fix before merge; and the advisory test gate is CONCERNS for the same reason. 4 notes: xmax is PG-internal (documented, optionally add upgrade caveat), OAuth email PII to PostHog matches the disclosed email/password posture, identify_with_set_once with empty FirstTouch is a documented style deviation, pub complete_oauth_flow is a documented in-process boundary consideration.
disclosed_followups_not_findings: login_succeeded is OAuth-scoped by design; email/password path deliberately skips capture (verified: process_login calls identify only).
No first-touch attribution on OAuth (UTM dies in the full-page redirect) — documented in code comment.
Cross-provider returning user = new signup (upsert keys on auth_user_id; pre-existing account model).
